newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Daewoo, Multichoice in joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo, Multichoice in joint venture.

text.p: Daewoo Electronics SA announced on Thursday it had established a joint venture with MultiChoice Africa aimed at promoting satellite television rentals in multi-unit dwellings.
It said the joint venture, to be known as Daewoo Satellite Systems, had been formed to increase the penetration of its Pace satellite equipment.
"This service...will offer an attractive and affordable alternative to the initial purchase outlay of such a system," the company said in a statement.
Daewoo said poor consumer demand for large household electrical goods was part of the reason for a four percent drop in its earnings to 6.4 cents per share in the year to December.

Chief executive Mike Bosworth said earnings had also been heavily eroded by a steep increase in finance costs to 19.4 million rand from 5.2 million rand after short-term borrowings jumped to 67.06 million rand from 26.11 million rand.
"Illegal imports of consumer electronic products put pressure on margins and volumes in the period under review," he said.
Bosworth said the only solution to this problem was the elimination of high duties and the consequent removal of the incentive for this practice.

Earlier, the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA) announced that sixteen of the country's leading manufacturers and distributors of electronic goods had signed a letter giving their support to government to stamp out tax evasion on import duties.
In some market segments, the CEA said as much as 90 percent of imports were evading duties, costing the government more than 260 million rand a year.
Bosworth said that because of Daewoo's high gearing level, the company was considering a 60 million rand preference share issue and had not declared a dividend for the period.
He said that the first six months of 1997 were expected to be particularly difficult for the company as inventory levels were corrected and discontinued lines were phased out.
Conditions were expected to improve in the second half of 1997.
"The prospect of a reduction in interest rates should also contribute to the growth in consumer demand," he added.
